description: Hand-labelled connection-discovery set (the eval harness, crates/b2-embed/evals/): for each anchor note, the corpus notes a human would say belong next to it — its topic-cluster mates. Scores `Vault::similar` (discover::candidates — the two-stage centroid shortlist + exact max-sim, GH #38), which the retrieval eval alone does NOT cover: note-to-note discovery is a different task from query-to-note search even over the same stored vectors. A hit = any `expected` path in the top candidates. An EMPTY `expected` marks a NEGATIVE anchor — a deliberate loner whose labelled answer is that nothing in the corpus relates — scoring suppression (does discovery say so, or serve strangers?) rather than rank; every candidate surfaced for one is junk by label (index-engine.md §3's quality-floor ruling, PR #145). A loner must be orthogonal to every topic cluster, to every distractor note (the three long ones, plus the cosmos/campus-life lexical-collision pair added for GH #157 — distractors, not anchors, because their deliberate `univers` stem collision makes a 'nothing relates' label for either one arguable), AND to the other loners, or the label is arguable — which is why the loners are laundry / chess / git / throat-singing and deliberately NOT money-adjacent (personal-finance.md is in the corpus). Throat-singing replaced watercolor-painting on 2026-08-11: the model scored watercolor ↔ stain-removal the strongest pair in the corpus — pigment suspended in water, both notes — which made the 'nothing relates' label arguable in exactly the way this description forbids, so the arguable loner was replaced rather than argued over. The corpus is unlinked, so no candidate is excluded by the 1-hop graph rule. GH #183 added a four-note MULTI-TOPIC family, the minimum shape that makes centroid-average ranking (the shipped order, index-engine.md §3) and best-passage ranking disagree — every note above this line is single-subject, where a note's centroid and its best chunk agree by construction, so none of them could ever exercise that disagreement. Each multi-topic note pairs an on-topic half (genuinely a cluster mate) with an off-topic half (genuinely unrelated, drawn from a craft/hobby domain used nowhere else in the corpus, so it drags the note's centroid away from its mates without becoming a plausible neighbor of anything else): `pour-over-and-pottery.md` puts the on-topic half FIRST (mate of `espresso.md`); `radio-and-sleep-debt.md` puts it SECOND (mate of `insomnia.md`) — chunk order should not change whether a mate is found; `tire-pressure-and-knots.md` gives the off-topic half roughly triple the on-topic half's length (mate of `bicycle.md`) — the case where the centroid is dragged furthest from the one relevant chunk; `running-and-aquarium.md` is the negative control — BOTH halves unrelated to every anchor, so a long multi-chunk note cannot be rewarded by suppression scoring just for being long. GH #189/#192 added the family's dilution extreme, the journal shape a real vault accumulates by default: `week-log.md` — seven mutually-unrelated hobby sections, exactly one of them (a lava-field day) a close mate of `volcano.md`, ~6:1 dilution. It is the acceptance test of the post-stage-2 discovery floor (#192): averaging that many disagreeing sections collapses its normalized centroid toward the corpus's shared direction (#189's measured hub effect), so a stage-1 centroid floor fails on it in both directions at once — its own gem suppressed, its centroid served to loner anchors on content it does not contain — and only a floor that judges the best passage can carry it. Its negative sibling (#189's `scattered-week.md`) stays out per the watercolor rule: two journal-shaped notes were measured as each other's strongest pair in the whole corpus because the first-person practice-log register is itself a topic to the model, which makes a 'nothing relates' label for a second journal arguable.
